notes.meaning: God announces a serious prophecy that will fall heavily on Israel's enemies but bring great comfort to His people. He presents Himself as the Creator who stretched out the sky, laid the earth's foundations, and formed the human spirit. Because the Lord constantly sustains all of creation, He has the unlimited power needed to keep His promises.

Hostile nations will surround Jerusalem like people eager to drink a cup of wine. Instead of victory, God will make the city like a cup of poison that makes the attackers stagger and collapse in ruin. The surrounding villages of Judah will be attacked as well, but the Lord will deliver them alongside the capital.

Jerusalem is compared to a massive stone that is far too heavy for anyone to move. All the nations of the earth may join together to clear it away, but they will only tear and crush themselves trying to lift it. God's kingdom cannot be shoved aside by human armies.

The attacking nations will rely on their powerful cavalry, but God will throw both horses and riders into panic, confusion, and blindness. In their terror, the enemy soldiers will lose their way and turn on one another. While the invaders fall apart, the Lord will watch over the people of Judah with loving care.

The leaders out in the countryside of Judah will realize that Jerusalem's real strength does not come from high walls or money. They recognize that the city stands firm because the Lord of hosts is their God. Seeing God's presence at work will unite all the people in shared faith.

God will give Judah's leaders supernatural strength to destroy their enemies like a firepot burning dry wood or a torch in a field of grain. The surrounding hostile armies will be quickly consumed by God's judgment. Through it all, the city of Jerusalem will remain secure and inhabited in its own place.

The Lord promises to rescue the open country homes and tents of Judah before saving the fortified city of Jerusalem. This ensures that the royal family and wealthy city dwellers cannot boast as though their power or status saved the day. God levels human pride so that everyone gives all credit to Him alone.

The Lord will shield everyone living in Jerusalem with extraordinary grace and courage. Even the weakest citizen who stumbles will fight as bravely as King David did against Goliath. The royal family will lead with divine strength, acting like the angel of the Lord who guided Israel in the wilderness.

God sets His purpose firmly to wipe out every enemy nation that attacks Jerusalem. When God says He will seek to destroy them, it means He is fully resolved and actively directing events to bring about their defeat. No earthly alliance can stand against His plan to defend His chosen people.

God promises to pour out His Holy Spirit upon leaders and ordinary people alike, giving them grace and prompting them to pray. They will look by faith upon the Lord Himself, whom they pierced, pointing to the crucifixion of Jesus Christ. This sight will bring deep and tender sorrow for sin, like parents mourning the death of an only child.

differ.view: This prophecy will be fully accomplished at the end of the age when the Jewish nation turns to Jesus right before His second coming.
This promise began to be fulfilled during the time of the apostles when many Jewish people turned to Christ and repented after hearing the gospel.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Some scholars propose that the pierced figure was not the Messiah but a historical prophet or martyr, such as Isaiah or Jeremiah.

notes.meaning: The mourning in Jerusalem over the pierced Savior will match the greatest public weeping in Israel's history. That took place at Hadad-rimmon near Megiddo, when the godly King Josiah was killed in battle. Just as the whole nation wept over losing their king, people will bitterly mourn the death of Christ.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Some scholars think Hadad-rimmon refers to a pagan mourning ritual for a Syrian or Canaanite deity rather than King Josiah's death.

notes.meaning: This deep sorrow for sin will spread through the whole land and reach every single home. The royal family of David and the priestly tribe of Levi are singled out to show that leaders and priests must repent just like everyone else. Each family and each spouse will mourn privately, showing that genuine repentance is a personal matter of the heart and not just a public show.
